motivation: Current AI lacks understanding of non-differentiable features in compressible flows, limiting spatiotemporal reconstruction accuracy.
method: The Inverse Low-Dimensional Manifold (ILDM) framework couples a Non-differentiable Approximation Function (NAF) for capturing shocks and a Smooth Fluid Reconstruction (SFR) module for smooth regions.
result: ILDM outperforms cPINN and R-adaptive DeepONet on 1D and 2D benchmarks, achieving superior localization of interfaces and robust super-resolution.
conclusion: ILDM provides a physically consistent and scalable paradigm for data-driven fluid dynamics reconstruction.

title: Zeros Of Gkp Sequences Of Polynomials
authors: Antonio J. Dur\'an, Mario P\'erez, Juan L. Varona
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06578v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given two sequences [MATH] and [MATH] and numbers [MATH], we introduce the GKP sequence of polynomials [MATH] using the following recurrence formula: [MATH] and for [MATH] \[ p_{n}(x) = (ax^2+bx+c) p_{n-1}'(x) + (\phi_{n} + \psi_{n} x)p_{n-1}(x), \] where we assume that [MATH] has two different real zeros. Tangent, Secant, Eulerian or Jacobi polynomials are examples of GKP sequences of polynomials. In this paper, under mild assumptions we prove that the zeros of the polynomials [MATH] are real, simple and live between the zeros of [MATH]. Moreover, the zeros of [MATH] interlace the zeros of [MATH]. We study in detail the cases when [MATH] is constant, and [MATH] is constant for [MATH] big enough, proving, among other results, asymptotics for the leftmost and rightmost zeros of [MATH].
tldr: This paper studies the zeros of GKP sequences of polynomials, a class of orthogonal polynomials defined by a specific recurrence relation.
motivation: To understand the properties of zeros of GKP polynomials, which generalize classical polynomial families like Tangent, Secant, Eulerian, and Jacobi polynomials.
method: The authors analyze the recurrence relation and use analytic techniques to prove that zeros are real, simple, and interlaced under mild assumptions.
result: They prove that zeros of GKP polynomials are real, simple, and lie between the zeros of the previous polynomial, with interlacing properties. Asymptotics for extreme zeros are also derived.
conclusion: The work provides a comprehensive characterization of zeros for a broad class of polynomials, contributing to the theory of orthogonal polynomials.

title: Picture Fuzzy Multigroups
authors: Taiwo O. Sangodapo
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06580v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, picture fuzzy multisets were studied together with their associated properties. We also introduced the concept of picture fuzzy multigroups and established some of their algebraic properties.
tldr: The paper introduces picture fuzzy multigroups, an algebraic structure combining picture fuzzy sets and multisets.
motivation: To extend the theory of fuzzy algebraic structures by incorporating picture fuzzy multisets.
method: Defines picture fuzzy multisets and their properties, then introduces picture fuzzy multigroups and studies their algebraic properties.
result: Establishes basic algebraic properties of picture fuzzy multigroups.
conclusion: The work contributes to fuzzy algebra but has no connection to quantum information theory or the user's research interests.

title: Stable Phase Retrieval For Spans Of Independent Random Variables
authors: Pedro Abdalla, Jaume de Dios Pont, Jo\~ao P. G. Ramos, Mitchell A. Taylor
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06693v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that, after [MATH] normalization, stable phase retrieval holds over the [MATH]-spans of independent real-valued centered random variables if and only if all but possibly one coordinate satisfies a uniform two-sided [MATH] bound. This provides a complete characterization of stable phase retrieval for such subspaces, building upon the pioneering work of Calderbank--Daubechies--Freeman--Freeman and confirming the conjectured characterization communicated to us by those authors. We provide two different proofs of this fact, both based on a decomposition of the [MATH]-coefficients of each random variable. The first is a compactness proof, which makes use of the infinite divisibility of limit laws of tail sums. The second is a quantitative proof, which substitutes the compactness step with an explicit dichotomy based on anticoncentration estimates of Sperner type. This latter proof was partially LLM generated based on the ideas in the first proof and a considerable amount of guidance by the authors. An autoformalization of our main result in Lean 4 is also provided, following the ideas in the quantitative proof.
tldr: This paper characterizes stable phase retrieval for spans of independent random variables, a problem in signal processing and harmonic analysis.
motivation: To determine necessary and sufficient conditions for stable phase retrieval in subspaces spanned by independent random variables, building on prior work.
method: Two proofs are given: a compactness argument using infinite divisibility of limit laws, and a quantitative proof using anticoncentration estimates of Sperner type.
result: Stable phase retrieval holds if and only if all but possibly one coordinate satisfies a uniform two-sided L^2 bound.
conclusion: The characterization is complete and confirmed by the authors of the original conjecture.

title: Expectation-Maximization Algorithm To Estimate The Forcing Parameter Of A Nonlinear McKean-Vlasov Diffusion
authors: Eduardo Gutierrez-Turner, Kerlyns Martinez, Hector Olivero
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06714v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we address the problem of estimating a forcing parameter in a stochastic differential equation inspired by a model that describes instantaneous turbulent kinetic energy. The stochastic differential equation we analyze is of the nonlinear McKean-Vlasov type, where the drift term depends on a power of the expected value of the solution, which also introduces nonlinearity in an algebraic sense. We propose an estimation algorithm based on the Expectation-Maximization framework and show the consistency of our method. We illustrate our findings through numerical experiments.
tldr: This paper proposes an Expectation-Maximization algorithm to estimate a forcing parameter in a nonlinear McKean-Vlasov diffusion model for turbulent kinetic energy.
motivation: Estimating parameters in stochastic differential equations with mean-field interactions is challenging; the authors aim to provide a consistent estimation method for a specific model inspired by turbulence.
method: The authors develop an EM-based algorithm that iteratively computes the conditional expectation of the complete-data log-likelihood and maximizes it to estimate the forcing parameter, leveraging the nonlinear McKean-Vlasov structure.
result: The algorithm is shown to be consistent, and numerical experiments demonstrate its effectiveness in recovering the true parameter.
conclusion: The proposed EM algorithm offers a viable approach for parameter estimation in nonlinear McKean-Vlasov diffusions, with potential applications in turbulence modeling.

title: AirPASS: Over-the-Air Federated Learning Via Pinching Antenna Systems
authors: Christopher G. Brinton Seyed Mohammad Azimi-Abarghouyi
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06768v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates over-the-air federated learning (AirFL) in wireless systems where the access point is equipped with a multi-waveguide pinching antenna system (PASS). We adopt the widely studied learning-oriented AirFL formulation, which seeks to maximize the number of selected devices while keeping the aggregation distortion below a prescribed threshold. The resulting joint optimization of device selection, receive beamforming, and pinching-antenna placement is highly nonconvex due to the intricate coupling among these system variables. To address this challenge, we develop AirPASS, an alternating optimization framework with two main components: a homotopy-Riemannian margin-consolidation method for device selection and receive beamforming under fixed PASS configuration, and a homotopy-assisted geometry optimization method for updating the pinching-antenna positions under fixed selected devices and beamformer. Experiments show that AirPASS consistently outperforms conventional co-located MIMO baselines, remains close to ideal FedAvg, and achieves an attractive performance-complexity tradeoff relative to SDR-DC and matching-pursuit scheduling alternatives.
tldr: This paper proposes an over-the-air federated learning framework using pinching antenna systems to optimize device selection, beamforming, and antenna placement.
motivation: Federated learning over wireless networks faces challenges from limited bandwidth and interference; over-the-air aggregation can reduce communication overhead but requires careful resource allocation.
method: The authors develop AirPASS, an alternating optimization framework combining homotopy-Riemannian margin-consolidation for device selection and beamforming, and homotopy-assisted geometry optimization for antenna placement.
result: AirPASS outperforms conventional MIMO baselines and achieves performance close to ideal FedAvg with favorable complexity tradeoffs.
conclusion: Pinching antenna systems can effectively support over-the-air federated learning, but the work is primarily a wireless communication and machine learning engineering contribution.

title: Cocentral Split Abelian Hopf Algebra Extensions From Crossed Cocycles
authors: Giovanny Mora C\'esar Galindo
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06865v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study cocentral split abelian Hopf algebra extensions over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. The kernel is [MATH] and the quotient is [MATH], where [MATH] is finite abelian and [MATH] acts on [MATH]. For a fixed action, we describe these extensions by crossed families of normalized group 2-cocycles on [MATH], modulo changes of homogeneous section. We give the obstruction to lifting cohomology classes to such cocycle data. Using the Schur multiplier of [MATH], we rewrite this obstruction as a bicharacter lifting problem; it vanishes when [MATH] has odd exponent. We then apply the theory to permutation modules and to arithmetic reductions of Coxeter modules, including explicit dihedral and rank-one affine examples.
tldr: This paper studies cocentral split abelian Hopf algebra extensions using crossed cocycles, focusing on algebraic structures with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to classify certain Hopf algebra extensions over algebraically closed fields, motivated by pure algebra and representation theory.
method: They describe extensions via crossed families of normalized group 2-cocycles, analyze obstructions using Schur multipliers, and apply the theory to permutation and Coxeter modules.
result: The obstruction to lifting cohomology classes is reformulated as a bicharacter lifting problem, which vanishes when the abelian group has odd exponent.
conclusion: The work provides a classification of these extensions and demonstrates applications to specific module examples, but remains entirely within pure mathematics.

title: A Study On Cumulative Residual Extropy Of Linear Consecutive k-out-of-n:G Systems
authors: Chanchal Kundu Aman Pandey
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06992v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we investigate the cumulative residual extropy associated with linear consecutive k-out-of-n:G systems, which play an important role in reliability theory and engineering applications. We first derive explicit expressions for the proposed measure and examine the behavior of cumulative residual extropy under a variety of stochastic orderings. In addition, several bounds and meaningful results of the characterization are established. Moreover, we also introduced the dynamic version of the cumulative residual extropy and explored the relationship between the proposed dynamic version and the mean residual life function. Fromaninferentialperspective, wedevelopanonparametricestimationprocedure for the cumulative residual extropy and establish the corresponding consistency properties of the estimator. The finite-sample performance of the proposed estimator is further investigated through extensive Monte Carlo simulation studies under different parametric settings and validated through a real dataset.
tldr: This paper studies cumulative residual extropy for linear consecutive k-out-of-n:G systems in reliability theory.
motivation: To extend the concept of cumulative residual extropy to a specific system structure and provide inferential tools.
method: Derives explicit expressions, examines stochastic orderings, establishes bounds and characterizations, and develops a nonparametric estimator with consistency properties.
result: Provides theoretical results and a consistent estimator, validated through simulations and a real dataset.
conclusion: The proposed measure and estimator are useful for reliability analysis of consecutive k-out-of-n:G systems.

title: Solution Analysis Of Tensor Equation $\mathcal{A} \ltimes \mathcal{X} \ltimes \mathcal{B}= \mathcal{C}$ Via Semi Tensor Product With T-product
authors: Ranjan Kumar Das Bhawna Garg
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07006v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper focuses on the analysis of the tensor equation [MATH], formulated via the semi tensor product with t-product. For the unknown vector [MATH], we establish a necessary and sufficient condition that provides an equivalence criterion for the existence of solutions. For matrix valued and higher-order tensor valued unknown [MATH], solvability is determined by corresponding compatibility requirements. Moreover, the explicit structure (Toeplitz and Circulant) of [MATH] is characterized. The derived results are supported by several illustrative examples.
tldr: This paper solves a tensor equation using semi-tensor product and t-product, focusing on solvability conditions and structural characterization.
motivation: To provide necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of solutions to a specific tensor equation, which is a mathematical problem in tensor algebra.
method: The authors use semi-tensor product with t-product to analyze the equation, establishing equivalence criteria for vector unknowns and compatibility requirements for matrix and higher-order tensor unknowns.
result: They derive explicit Toeplitz and Circulant structures for the solution and provide illustrative examples.
conclusion: The work contributes to the theory of tensor equations but has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Mixed Precision Explicit Numerical Methods For Ordinary Differential Equations
authors: M Al Sayed Ali (BIOTIC, MUSICS), S Bernard (BIOTIC, MUSICS), A Marzorati (MMCS, MUSICS, ICJ, BIOTIC), J Rouzaud-Cornabas
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07080v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Our objective is to solve large systems of ordinary differential equations (ODEs) commonly used to model biological processes. These equations are typically nonlinear, complex, and high-dimensional. In computational biology, such ODEs are generally solved using numerical methods. In this work, we focus on explicit numerical methods because of their flexibility. However, their limited stability regions may result in high computational costs. To mitigate this issue, we investigate mixed precision algorithms designed to reduce computational effort by performing selected parts of the numerical method in lower arithmetic precision. We develop several mixed precision explicit methods and assess their performance on two large scale biological benchmark ODE models. Our theoretical analysis highlights the effectiveness of partially reducing arithmetic precision within explicit methods. Numerical experiments demonstrate that our mixed methods-implemented in both sequential and parallel versions using MPI-combining single (float) and double precision arithmetic can achieve up to twice the speed of a fully double precision implementation while preserving the same level of accuracy. Furthermore, the results indicate that decreasing the timestep improves the performance and robustness of our mixed methods, while the single precision method fails to converge.
tldr: This paper develops mixed precision explicit numerical methods for solving large systems of ODEs in computational biology, achieving speedup while maintaining accuracy.
motivation: Solving large ODE systems in computational biology is computationally expensive due to limited stability regions of explicit methods.
method: The authors propose mixed precision algorithms that use lower precision for selected parts of explicit numerical methods, implemented in sequential and parallel (MPI) versions.
result: Mixed precision methods achieve up to twice the speed of double precision implementations while preserving accuracy, and decreasing timestep improves performance.
conclusion: Mixed precision explicit methods are effective for reducing computational cost in large-scale ODE simulations without sacrificing accuracy.

title: The Chain Graph Of A General Iterated Function System
authors: Roberto de Leo
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07112v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Classical fractal geometry describes the metric and topological structure of attractors generated by contractive Iterated Function Systems (IFSs). Much less is known about their global qualitative dynamics once the contractive hypothesis is abandoned. In this article we focus on IFSs with "compact dynamics", namely those IFSs for which there exists a non-empty compact set invariant under the Hutchinson map that attracts every compact subset of the phase space. We call such a set the "global attractor" of the IFS. We introduce the "chain graph" of a general IFS as a directed graph encoding the qualitative dynamics features of the IFS. For an IFS with compact dynamics, the chain graph contains at least one node. Our main results are that the chain graph of an IFS with compact dynamics coincides with the chain graph of its restriction to its global attractor and that the chain graph of an IFS has at most as many nodes as the graph of its Hutchinson map.
tldr: This paper studies the global qualitative dynamics of iterated function systems without contractive hypothesis, introducing the concept of chain graph.
motivation: Classical fractal geometry focuses on contractive IFSs; this work aims to understand the dynamics when contractivity is abandoned.
method: The authors define the chain graph of a general IFS and analyze its properties for IFSs with compact dynamics.
result: The chain graph of an IFS with compact dynamics coincides with that of its restriction to the global attractor, and its number of nodes is bounded by the graph of the Hutchinson map.
conclusion: The chain graph provides a tool to encode qualitative dynamics of IFSs beyond the contractive case.

title: The Technological Turn In Mathematics
authors: Fenner Tanswell Silvia de Toffoli
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07162v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quickly evolving technologies, such as Interactive Theorem Provers (ITPs), Automated Theorem Provers (ATPs), and Large Language Models (LLMs), all falling under the general heading 'AI for mathematics,' are transforming mathematical practice in profound ways. This chapter explores the implications of these innovations, focusing on their impact on how mathematical knowledge is created and shared. It also discusses how they are reshaping the social dimension of mathematics, altering collaboration dynamics, trust relationships, and the collective production of knowledge. For instance, tools like ITPs facilitate large-scale collaborations and make new types of teamwork possible, where trust is not a necessary ingredient. ITPs also help us mitigate our human fallibility, yet they raise questions about the nature of formalization and the relationship between traditional and formal mathematics. Technologies such as LLMs are reshaping the division of epistemic labour between humans and machines and urge philosophers of mathematics to ask questions about the value of their work.
tldr: This paper discusses the impact of AI and theorem provers on mathematical practice, not quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to explore how technologies like ITPs, ATPs, and LLMs are transforming mathematical knowledge creation and collaboration.
method: The paper is a philosophical and sociological analysis of current trends in mathematical practice, drawing on examples and case studies.
result: It identifies shifts in collaboration dynamics, trust relationships, and the division of epistemic labor between humans and machines.
conclusion: The paper argues that these technologies are reshaping mathematics in profound ways, raising new philosophical questions.

title: Stochastic Inversion Of Multivariate Uniform-Distribution-Preserving Transformations
authors: Johanna G. Ne\v{s}lehov\'a Alexander J. Mcneil
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07174v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A multivariate transformation of the unit cube with component transformations that are piecewise continuously differentiable and uniform distribution preserving (udp) is considered. A stochastic inverse transformation is defined using randomization to overcome the non-injective nature of the udp transformations. The inverse transformation preserves the uniform margins of a random vector distributed according to a copula and yields different copulas for different randomizations. A copula density transformation result for the multivariate stochastic inverse is proved and illustrated in the bivariate case.
tldr: This paper studies stochastic inversion of multivariate uniform-distribution-preserving transformations and its effect on copulas.
motivation: To handle non-injective uniform-distribution-preserving transformations by defining a stochastic inverse that preserves uniform margins.
method: Uses randomization to define a stochastic inverse transformation and proves a copula density transformation result.
result: The stochastic inverse preserves uniform margins and yields different copulas for different randomizations.
conclusion: The work provides a mathematical framework for stochastic inversion in the context of copulas, but has no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: The Randomized Bh Procedure: A Generalized Framework Encompassing Conformal And Competition Tests
authors: Yan Fu Mingzhou Deng
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07245v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose the Randomized BH procedure, a generalized framework that introduces randomization into the Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) procedure for false discovery rate (FDR) control. We show that the classical BH procedure as well as two recently developed families of null-distribution-free methods, competition tests and conformal tests, share a common theoretical foundation and arise as special cases of this framework. The Randomized BH relaxes the classical conditions required for FDR control, frees conformal tests from the strict exchangeability assumption while allowing calibration sets to be constructed via pre-screening, and enables competition tests to be analyzed through the well-developed theory of p-values. We illustrate the framework through two applications. The first is a deeper analysis of compound p-values through the lens of randomization. The second is a general approach for integrating distributed multiple testing problems while maintaining global FDR control. Numerical simulations confirm the validity of our theoretical results.
tldr: This paper proposes a randomized framework for false discovery rate control in multiple testing, with applications to conformal and competition tests.
motivation: To generalize the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure and unify conformal and competition tests under a common theoretical framework.
method: Introduces randomization into the BH procedure and shows that classical BH, competition tests, and conformal tests are special cases.
result: The Randomized BH procedure relaxes exchangeability assumptions for conformal tests and enables p-value-based analysis for competition tests.
conclusion: The framework provides a unified approach to FDR control with broader applicability.

title: Gradient-free Stochastic Optimization Of Derivatives Under Strong Convexity
authors: Arya Akhavan, Sirine Louati, Alexandre B. Tsybakov
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07249v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the problem of minimizing the [MATH]-th order partial derivative [MATH] of an unknown function [MATH] along a fixed coordinate direction [MATH], based on noisy queries of [MATH]. Assuming that [MATH] has H\"older regularity [MATH] for some [MATH], that [MATH] is strongly convex on a compact convex set [MATH] and that [MATH] and [MATH] satisfy mild boundedness and Lipschitz regularity conditions on [MATH], we propose a kernel-based estimator of [MATH] and analyze the projected stochastic gradient algorithm driven by this estimator. We obtain a non-asymptotic upper bound on the optimization error of the order [MATH], where [MATH] is the total number of queries. We also establish a minimax lower bound of the order [MATH] showing that this rate is optimal in [MATH] over all sequential algorithms.
tldr: This paper studies gradient-free stochastic optimization of derivatives under strong convexity, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to minimize a partial derivative of an unknown function using noisy queries, which is a problem in classical optimization.
method: They propose a kernel-based estimator and analyze a projected stochastic gradient algorithm driven by this estimator.
result: They derive non-asymptotic upper and minimax lower bounds on the optimization error, showing optimality in the number of queries.
conclusion: The work provides optimal rates for derivative optimization under strong convexity, but it is purely classical and unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: Mathematical Models For Car T Immunotherapy And Cd19 Dynamics In Leukemia: A Comparative Analysis
authors: Salvador Chuli\'an, Ana Ni\~no-L\'opez, Roc\'io Pic\'on-Gonz\'alez, Mar\'ia Rosa
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07261v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chimeric Antigen Receptor (CAR) T cell therapy has emerged as a successful treatment for relapsed or refractory hematological malignancies, particularly for B cell Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (B ALL), where CD19 targeted therapies have achieved high initial remission rates. However, relapse after treatment remains a major clinical challenge, frequently associated with antigen escape mechanisms and the emergence of CD19[MATH] leukemic cells. Understanding the interaction between CAR T cells and antigen expression dynamics is, therefore, essential for improving therapeutic efficacy and long-term patient outcomes. In this work, we develop and comparatively analyze novel mathematical models describing CAR T immunotherapy and CD19 dynamics in leukemia. Our proposed framework combines compartmental ordinary differential equation (ODE) formulations as well as partial differential equation (PDE) systems. Both methods are able to capture the evolution of leukemic populations under immune pressure and, in particular, the models explicitly distinguish between CD19[MATH] and CD19[MATH] leukemic cells and incorporate bidirectional phenotypic transitions regulated by CAR T activity. The developed models provide biologically interpretable and computationally efficient tools for studying treatment response, resistance, and relapse mechanisms in CAR T cell therapy. We compare the ability of the different modeling approaches to reproduce CD19 antigen modulation and CAR T efficacy dynamics. We also propose sensitivity analyses to study the parameters' influence on the models' dynamics. Our work contributes to the mathematical understanding of antigen-driven resistance and offers a basis for future optimization and personalization of CAR T therapeutic strategies in leukemia.
tldr: This paper develops mathematical models for CAR T cell immunotherapy and CD19 dynamics in leukemia, focusing on antigen escape and relapse mechanisms.
motivation: Relapse after CAR T therapy remains a major challenge, often due to antigen escape. Understanding CAR T and antigen dynamics is essential for improving treatment.
method: The authors propose compartmental ODE and PDE models that distinguish CD19+ and CD19- leukemic cells and incorporate bidirectional phenotypic transitions regulated by CAR T activity.
result: The models capture leukemic population evolution under immune pressure and reproduce CD19 antigen modulation and CAR T efficacy dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides biologically interpretable tools for studying resistance and relapse, offering a basis for optimizing CAR T strategies.

title: The Strong Stability Of The Perron-Frobenius Semigroup And Almost Global Attractivity
authors: George Weiss Pietro Lorenzetti
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07331v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We discuss some useful properties of the solution map (flow) of a nonlinear dynamical system with a finite-dimensional state space. Then, we introduce the Perron-Frobenius semigroup, and we prove that it is a positive strongly continuous semigroup of contractions. We show that, given a nonlinear system and an invariant set, this set is an almost global attractor if and only if certain Perron-Frobenius semigroups associated to the nonlinear system are strongly stable. Unlike other works on the Perron-Frobenius semigroup from the literature, we do not require the existence of a compact and invariant state-space for the dynamical system, we allow trajectories with finite escape time, and we do not require the attractor to be locally (Lyapunov) stable. Two simple examples are used throughout the paper to illustrate the theory.
tldr: This paper studies the strong stability of the Perron-Frobenius semigroup and its relation to almost global attractivity in nonlinear dynamical systems.
motivation: To characterize almost global attractors using the stability of Perron-Frobenius semigroups without requiring compact invariant state spaces or local stability.
method: The authors prove that the Perron-Frobenius semigroup is a positive strongly continuous contraction semigroup and establish a necessary and sufficient condition for almost global attractivity in terms of strong stability of the semigroup.
result: An invariant set is an almost global attractor if and only if certain Perron-Frobenius semigroups are strongly stable, generalizing previous results.
conclusion: The theory applies to systems with finite escape time and without local stability, illustrated by two examples.

title: The Power Of Backdoor Absorption In Community Training
authors: Issam Seddik, Sami Souihi, Mohamed Tamaazousti, Sara Tucci Piergiovanni
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06643v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Backdoor attacks severely threaten large-scale AI models. When model owners delegate training to external compute providers within a decentralized training paradigm, adversaries can craft stealthy, low-frequency triggers to inject malicious behavior while evading standard audits. Traditionally, detecting these attacks requires a full re-computation of the training steps--a prohibitive overhead that directly contradicts the owner's resource constraints. To address this, we investigate the resilience of continuous optimization dynamics under Byzantine perturbations, where adversaries are forced to compete against a continuous influx of honest updates. Under a threat model where an adversary compromises f out of n total trainers, we quantify the minimum auditing overhead required by the model owner to probabilistically bound the attack success rate. We formalize this injection-absorption dynamic as a Discrete-Time Markov Chain (DTMC). Using this framework, we prove that the success probability of any bounded adversary asymptotically collapses to zero under a defense strategy combining natural absorption, a randomized scheduler, and lazy verification oracle. Empirical results demonstrate significant backdoor suppression with zero utility degradation even when invoking the verification oracle on merely 10% of the total training steps. This approach yields a provably sound and computationally efficient defense for safety-critical AI.
tldr: This paper proposes a defense against backdoor attacks in decentralized training using a Markov chain model and lazy verification.
motivation: Backdoor attacks threaten large-scale AI models, and existing defenses require prohibitive computational overhead.
method: The authors model the attack-defense dynamic as a Discrete-Time Markov Chain and prove that a combination of natural absorption, randomized scheduling, and lazy verification collapses attack success probability to zero.
result: Empirical results show significant backdoor suppression with zero utility degradation using only 10% verification steps.
conclusion: The proposed defense is provably sound and computationally efficient for safety-critical AI.

title: Fixed Points, A Predictor-Impossibility Theorem, And Applications
authors: Tom Altman
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06956v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce an activation hierarchy consisting of stage machines, stage domains, and stage languages generated by an activation operator. The central result is a Predictor-Impossibility Theorem (PIT), which shows that no effective predictor family can uniformly determine all stage languages of the hierarchy. The proof combines the semantic activation construction with the S-m-n Theorem and Kleene's Recursion Theorem to obtain a self-referential fixed point that yields a contradiction. We then define an aggregate language MIS and establish a slice theorem connecting aggregate inputs to individual stage languages. This provides a bridge from polynomial-time decidability of MIS to the existence of a predictor family. By PIT, the aggregate language is, therefore, not polynomial-time decidable. Under the aggregate growth condition defining valid aggregate objects, MIS is shown to belong to NP. Combining these two results yields MIS in NP-P. The paper is organized so that PIT stands independently as a recursion-theoretic result, while the complexity-theoretic consequences are derived from the aggregate-language framework.
tldr: The paper proves a Predictor-Impossibility Theorem using recursion theory and shows that a certain aggregate language is in NP but not P.
motivation: To establish fundamental limits on prediction and to separate NP from P via a novel recursion-theoretic construction.
method: Introduces an activation hierarchy with stage machines and languages, uses the S-m-n Theorem and Kleene's Recursion Theorem to derive a fixed-point contradiction.
result: No effective predictor family can uniformly determine all stage languages, and the aggregate language MIS is in NP but not polynomial-time decidable.
conclusion: The work provides a recursion-theoretic impossibility result with complexity-theoretic consequences, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Large Language Models (LLMs) And Generative Ai In Cybersecurity And Privacy: A Survey Of Dual-Use Risks, AI-Generated Malware, Explainability, And Defensive Strategies
authors: Saeed Valizadeh Kiarash Ahi
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06963v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) and generative AI (GenAI) systems, such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, LLaMA, Copilot, Stable Diffusion by OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, Microsoft, Stability AI, respectively, are revolutionizing cybersecurity, enabling both automated defense and sophisticated attacks. These technologies power real-time threat detection, phishing defense, secure code generation, and vulnerability exploitation at unprecedented scales. Following a rapid surge where LLM-generated malware grew to account for an estimated 50% of detected threats by 2025, up from just 2% in 2021, navigating this highly automated threat landscape in 2026 demands next-generation security frameworks. This paper presents a comprehensive survey of the beneficial and malicious applications of LLMs in cybersecurity, including zero-day detection, DevSecOps, federated learning, synthetic content analysis, and explainable AI (XAI). Drawing on a review of over 70 academic papers, industry reports, and technical documents, this work synthesizes insights from real-world case studies across platforms like Google Play Protect, Microsoft Defender, Amazon Web Services (AWS), Apple App Store, OpenAI Plugin Stores, Hugging Face Spaces, and GitHub, alongside emerging initiatives like the SAFE Framework and AI-driven anomaly detection. We conclude with practical recommendations for responsible and transparent LLM deployment and trustworthy AI, including model watermarking, adversarial defense, and cross-industry collaboration, setting a new benchmark for rigorous, holistic cybersecurity research at the intersection of AI and threat defense, and offering a roadmap for secure, scalable LLM systems that serves as a critical reference for researchers, engineers, and security leaders navigating the complex challenges of AI-driven cybersecurity.
tldr: A survey of dual-use risks of LLMs and generative AI in cybersecurity, covering both defensive and offensive applications.
motivation: The rapid growth of LLM-generated malware and AI-driven attacks necessitates a comprehensive understanding of both beneficial and malicious uses of these technologies in cybersecurity.
method: The paper reviews over 70 academic papers, industry reports, and technical documents, synthesizing insights from real-world case studies across major platforms.
result: It identifies key dual-use risks, including AI-generated malware, and discusses defensive strategies such as model watermarking, adversarial defense, and explainable AI.
conclusion: The paper provides recommendations for responsible LLM deployment and sets a benchmark for holistic cybersecurity research at the intersection of AI and threat defense.

title: What Semivalues Cannot See: The Information Content Of Anonymous Marginal Values
authors: Matthew Fried
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07013v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The semivalue family shares a common kernel: games invisible to every anonymous marginal value at once, nonzero from four players (Kleinberg and Weiss, 1985; Amer, Derks and Gim\'enez, 2003). Crisman and Orrison (2015) ask what useful structure this kernel carries; this paper gives a concrete answer. In Harsanyi-dividend coordinates the joint information of all semivalues is exactly each player's total synergy at each coalition size, so the kernel is synergy arranged in closed circuits. We prove: order-[MATH] mixed-difference audits recover exactly the degree-[MATH] dividend-slice harmonics, with closed-form dimension at every rung; nonzero blind games fail superadditivity, monotonicity, and core existence, yet distinct convex games with identical values under every semivalue exist from four players, with exact perturbation thresholds; the positive weighted Shapley family attains full information [MATH], so anonymity is the binding axiom within the marginal framework; and a coalition of size [MATH] defeats every audit of order [MATH] precisely when [MATH], within the convex class for small perturbations. An exhaustive census at [MATH] exhibits non-isomorphic voting rules with identical values under every semivalue power index; no weighted game participates in any collision, prompting a swing-rigidity conjecture. Measured against the theory, classical cooperative games sit at [MATH] to [MATH] visibility to the family versus [MATH] for a random game.
tldr: This paper studies the kernel of semivalues in cooperative game theory, showing that the joint information of all semivalues captures synergy at each coalition size, and that anonymous marginal values cannot distinguish certain games.
motivation: To understand what structure is carried by the kernel of semivalues—games invisible to all anonymous marginal values—and to answer a question posed by Crisman and Orrison about its usefulness.
method: The paper uses Harsanyi-dividend coordinates to analyze the information content of semivalues, and employs combinatorial and algebraic methods to characterize the kernel and its properties.
result: The kernel consists of synergy arranged in closed circuits; nonzero blind games fail superadditivity, monotonicity, and core existence; distinct convex games with identical semivalues exist from four players; and a coalition of size m defeats every audit of order k precisely when m > k.
conclusion: The kernel of semivalues has a concrete structure related to synergy circuits, and anonymity is the binding axiom within the marginal framework, with implications for voting power indices.

title: Is Randomness Necessary For Adaptive Data Analysis?
authors: Edith Cohen, Haim Kaplan, Yishay Mansour, Shay Sapir, Uri Stemmer
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07085v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Adaptive Data Analysis (ADA) problem formalizes the challenge of preventing false discovery and overfitting when a dataset is repeatedly reused. Formally, our input is a dataset containing [MATH] i.i.d. samples from an unknown distribution [MATH] over a domain [MATH], and our goal is to answer a sequence of [MATH] adaptively chosen statistical queries with respect to [MATH]. The main question is how many queries we can support (i.e., how large [MATH] can be), primarily as a function of the number of samples [MATH]. This question has been intensively studied and is relatively well-understood for randomized mechanisms: there are computationally efficient mechanisms that support [MATH] queries, and no computationally efficient mechanism can answer [MATH] queries. In this paper, we address a fundamental question: is randomness necessary for ADA? Despite a decade of work on ADA, this question remains open. A folklore observation dating back to the initial works on ADA is that randomness is not necessary when the analyst is computationally bounded. Yet, the necessity of randomness against computationally unbounded analysts has remained elusive. Our main contribution resolves this gap in the information-theoretic Random Oracle model. Perhaps surprisingly, we show that randomness is strictly necessary to answer a non-trivial number of adaptive queries: when the analyst is unbounded, any deterministic mechanism can be forced to fail after just [MATH] queries.
tldr: This paper studies whether randomness is necessary for adaptive data analysis, proving that deterministic mechanisms fail after a small number of queries in the random oracle model.
motivation: The adaptive data analysis problem aims to prevent false discovery when reusing a dataset, and while randomized mechanisms are well-understood, the necessity of randomness against computationally unbounded analysts was an open question.
method: The authors prove a lower bound in the information-theoretic random oracle model, showing that any deterministic mechanism can be forced to fail after O(log n) queries.
result: Randomness is strictly necessary for answering a non-trivial number of adaptive queries when the analyst is computationally unbounded.
conclusion: The work resolves a fundamental gap in adaptive data analysis, establishing that randomness is essential for robustness against unbounded adversaries.

title: Certifying Ghosts: How Cybersecurity Ai Agents Break The Eu Cyber Resilience Act
authors: V\'ictor Mayoral-Vilches
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07109v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) makes a smart bet. It does not demand that products be free of vulnerabilities, but only that manufacturers run a process: assess risk, handle flaws, ship updates. The bet pays off if four things about the world stay true: (P1) finding vulnerabilities is slow, skilled, human work; (P2) a product's exploitable flaws are knowable the day it ships; (P3) exploitation is rare enough to notice; and (P4) fixes keep pace with discovery. Cybersecurity AI (CAI) agents, AI put to work finding and exploiting flaws in other products, falsify all four. The regime answers in two opposite ways. Against the sheer volume of flaws that agents surface it bends (P1): built for scarce attention, it re-centres compliance on defensible, documented prioritisation, and holds. But agents also collapse the speed and economics of the vulnerability lifecycle, and here it breaks (P2, P3, P4): a product that passed every check becomes exploitable without anyone touching it, so its market-entry test, its reporting trigger, and its one-and-done certificate vouch for a security that has quietly expired. The fault is in the landscape, not the product, so running the process more diligently cannot repair it. We map each mechanism to the force that strains or snaps it, and find the cure and the disease cut from the same cloth: because defenders and attackers wield the same AI, the only conformity that survives is one that never stops running. We also carry the remedy from proposal to proof on two CRA-scope robots, a humanoid and a lawn mower, where an agentic defender holds a line their undefended selves cannot. On the evidence already in hand, the CRA reaches full force in December 2027 certifying products against a world that has already changed. Static, human-paced security is finished; what replaces it must be continuous and agent-operated, and that is no longer a matter of taste.
tldr: The paper analyzes how cybersecurity AI agents undermine the assumptions of the EU Cyber Resilience Act, arguing that static security certification is obsolete.
motivation: The EU Cyber Resilience Act relies on assumptions about vulnerability discovery and exploitation that are invalidated by AI-driven cybersecurity agents.
method: The authors identify four key premises of the CRA and show how AI agents falsify each, then propose a continuous, agent-operated security model.
result: AI agents can find and exploit vulnerabilities at a speed and scale that breaks the CRA's certification and reporting framework.
conclusion: Static, human-paced security certification is no longer viable; continuous, AI-driven security is necessary.

title: MoLIFE: Methodology, Technologies, And Challenges For Mobile Live Intelligent Forensics Examination
authors: Silvia Lucia Sanna, Cristina Alcaraz, Alessandro Sanna, Giorgio Giacinto, Javier Lopez
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07269v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nowadays, mobile forensics is less explored in Digital Forensics case analysis due to the increase in data protection mechanisms implemented by tech companies (i.e., Google for Android and Apple for iOS). For example, the physical acquisition or analysis of specific directories under super-user protection would corrupt the evidence; access to such data is protected, and bypassing this protection requires either privilege escalation or custom ROM installation, leading to the modification of the device state. At the same time, the demand for mobile technologies and their respective communication systems is increasing exponentially, exposing numerous security threats and risks. For that reason, this paper presents a Mobile Live Intelligent Forensics Examination (MoLIFE), a novel Digital Forensics (DF) methodology for data acquisition and analysis of mobile devices. The proposed methodology is based on NIST SP800-101 for the DF process. MoLIFE can be integrated with new and emerging technologies by exploiting their power (e.g., AI, blockchain, quantum computing). MoLIFE can also be used to prevent cyber threats and incidents, as well as DF post-mortem analysis, offering examples of applying the MoLIFE methodology and good practices for the future. To prove the technical feasibility of the methodology, a small case study on Android devices data acquisition via the mDT will be presented. As the methodology is based on new and emerging technologies, it depends on their limitations that would be overcome in a few years.
tldr: This paper presents a mobile live intelligent forensics examination methodology that mentions quantum computing as an emerging technology but does not engage with quantum information theory.
motivation: Mobile forensics faces challenges due to data protection mechanisms; the authors propose a new methodology to address these challenges.
method: The methodology is based on NIST SP800-101 and integrates AI, blockchain, and quantum computing as potential future enhancements; a case study on Android devices is presented.
result: The methodology is technically feasible for data acquisition on Android devices via the mDT tool.
conclusion: MoLIFE can be used for cyber threat prevention and post-mortem analysis, but its reliance on emerging technologies means limitations remain.

title: -8 dB Snr + 90% Packet Loss: MamVSC -- CSI-Guided Semantic Mamba For Extreme-Robust Video Semantic Communication
authors: Lei Teng, Senran Fan, Chen Dong, Haotai Liang, Xiaodong Xu, Ping Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07293v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Semantic communication, leveraging joint source-channel coding, is designed to mitigate semantic distortion introduced by the channel. However, most current studies focus solely on semantic deviation distortion caused by physical wireless channels, while overlooking semantic erasure distortion due to packet loss. A CSI-Guided Mamba-based video semantic wireless digital communication system (MamVSC) employing semantic grouping is proposed to simultaneously address both semantic deviation and erasure distortions. In this system, a semantic Mamba module, guided by channel state information (CSI) feedback, is utilized to dynamically adjust the granularity of extracted semantic information, adapting to channel conditions. Furthermore, a Semantic Channel Codec based on dynamic Semantic clustering centers is introduced, where the distance between semantic vectors within the same semantic class and their corresponding Semantic clustering center is dynamically adjusted according to channel conditions, enhancing robustness against channel noise. Additionally, a adaptive packet loss recovery module, dynamically adaptive to the CSI, is proposed. The system achieves an MS-SSIM greater than 0.6 and a PSNR exceeding 21 dB at an SNR of -8 dB and a packet loss rate of 90% in AWGN channel.
tldr: This paper proposes a video semantic communication system using Mamba and CSI guidance to handle both channel noise and packet loss.
motivation: Existing semantic communication methods focus on semantic deviation from channel noise but ignore semantic erasure due to packet loss.
method: A CSI-guided Mamba module dynamically adjusts semantic granularity, a semantic channel codec uses dynamic clustering centers, and an adaptive packet loss recovery module is introduced.
result: The system achieves MS-SSIM > 0.6 and PSNR > 21 dB at -8 dB SNR and 90% packet loss in AWGN channel.
conclusion: The proposed MamVSC system effectively addresses both semantic deviation and erasure distortions, showing extreme robustness.

title: zk-ScalHard: Scalable And Hardware-Rooted Privacy-Preserving Authentication For Secure Ota Updates In Zonal SDVs
authors: Shrikant Tangade, Bansi Pambhar, Valeria Loscri, Mauro Conti
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07371v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The automotive industry is transitioning to Zonal-oriented Architectures (ZoA) for Software-Defined Vehicles (SDVs), enabling frequent over-the-air (OTA) updates for 100+ Electronic Control Units (ECUs). While OTA updates improve efficiency, they introduce safety-critical security risks. Current standards like Uptane and AUTOSAR Adaptive rely on Public-Key Infrastructure (PKI). However, PKI-based authentication creates bandwidth bottlenecks in in-vehicle and vehicle-to-cloud (V2I) communication as ECU density increases. It also risks exposing sensitive vehicle configurations and passenger privacy due to centralized architectures. Next-generation Zonal SDVs require decentralized, scalable authentication with data privacy. To address this, we propose zk-ScalHard, a hardware-rooted, privacy-preserving authentication protocol. We introduce a decentralized, hierarchical trust-promotion model utilizing Silicon Physical Unclonable Functions (PUFs) and two novel Zero-Knowledge Proof (ZKP) circuits: (1) Zonal Identity and Integrity (ZIDI) and (2) High-Performance Computing Aggregation (HPCA). These circuits employ multi-party computation (MPC) and recursive aggregation to achieve decentralization and scalability. The integration of ZKPs and PUFs ensures 100% vehicle-level data sovereignty. Benchmarked against Uptane, zk-ScalHard achieves constant O(1) communication and verification complexity, improving upon the linear O(n) complexity of current systems. Evaluation shows a 99.2% reduction in authentication bandwidth and a 99.9% reduction in the temporal attack surface. Our results demonstrate that zk-ScalHard provides a scalable, secure, and GDPR-compliant architecture for future Zonal SDVs.
tldr: A privacy-preserving authentication protocol for OTA updates in zonal SDVs using PUFs and zero-knowledge proofs.
motivation: Current PKI-based authentication creates bandwidth bottlenecks and privacy risks in zonal SDVs with many ECUs.
method: Proposes zk-ScalHard with hierarchical trust model using silicon PUFs and two novel ZKP circuits (ZIDI and HPCA) for decentralized authentication.
result: Achieves O(1) communication and verification complexity, 99.2% reduction in authentication bandwidth, and 99.9% reduction in temporal attack surface.
conclusion: zk-ScalHard provides scalable, secure, and GDPR-compliant authentication for future zonal SDVs.

title: Positional Determinacy With Colored Vertices: A 1-to-2-Player Lift
authors: St\'ephane Le Roux Rapha\"el Berthon
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07415v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Positional determinacy of vertex-colored parity games was proved in the 1990s, which directly implies positional determinacy of edge-colored parity games. In 2006, it was shown that if a prefix-independent color-based objective ensures that every edge-colored two-player turn-based game is positionally determined, this objective is equivalent to a parity objective. We prove a similar result for vertex-colored games, namely that the following are equivalent for any prefix-independent objective [MATH] over a finite set of colors: - [MATH] is positionally determined on all vertex-colored one-player games. - [MATH] is positionally determined on all vertex-colored two-player games. - [MATH] is equivalent to a parity objective on ordrerd pairs of colors. We prove that finiteness of the color set is required for our equivalence to hold. Beyond this [MATH]-to-[MATH]-player lift, the technique that we develop to handle the pairs of colors establishes a promising 2-way correspondence between edge-colored games and vertex-colored games.
tldr: This paper proves an equivalence between positional determinacy in one-player and two-player vertex-colored parity games, showing that a prefix-independent objective is positionally determined on all vertex-colored one-player games iff it is equivalent to a parity objective on ordered pairs of colors.
motivation: The paper aims to extend known results about edge-colored parity games to vertex-colored games, establishing a 1-to-2-player lift for positional determinacy.
method: The authors develop a technique to handle pairs of colors and establish a correspondence between edge-colored and vertex-colored games, proving the equivalence via combinatorial arguments.
result: They prove that for any prefix-independent objective over a finite set of colors, positional determinacy on all vertex-colored one-player games implies positional determinacy on all vertex-colored two-player games, and that such objectives are equivalent to a parity objective on ordered pairs of colors.
conclusion: The finiteness of the color set is necessary for the equivalence, and the technique provides a promising 2-way correspondence between edge-colored and vertex-colored games.

title: Embedded Blockchain Infrastructure Management (eBIM): A RISC-V-Empowered Hardware--Software Co-Design Framework Towards Trustworthy Blockchain
authors: Qinglin Yang, Yuan Liu, Yaoyao Zhang, Boya Wang, Zongjian You, Chunming Rong, Zhihong Tian
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07625v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Blockchain systems are undergoing a fundamental transition from decentralized ledgers for digital assets to general-purpose trust infrastructures for verifiable computation, decentralized physical resources, and automated infrastructure management. Meanwhile, the limitations of the Blockchain as a Service (BaaS) model stem from a common structural problem: outsourcing control of infrastructure to third-party service providers inevitably involves a systemic surrender of trust, flexibility, and data sovereignty. RISC-V, with its open, modular, and extensible design, provides a general-purpose computing foundation for public blockchains that is open, low-level, compileable, verifiable, and scalable. Inspired by the development and characteristics of eSIM, the embedded Blockchain infrastructure management (eBIM) is defined as a software-hardware collaborative paradigm for blockchain infrastructure management with RISC-V. This study aims to provide a comprehensive survey on eBIM supporting research and technologies, to answer the following research questions (RQs): RQ1 What is eBIM? RQ2 How does eBIM work? RQ3 What can eBIM do? By introducing the concept of eBIM, this paper establishes a foundational reference for researchers, hardware architects, and protocol designers in this rapidly evolving landscape, including cryptographic acceleration, trusted execution environments, zero-knowledge virtual machines, and smart contract execution engines. The prospects of the proposed e-BIM and its future research directions are indicated in this paper.
tldr: This paper proposes eBIM, a hardware-software co-design framework using RISC-V for trustworthy blockchain infrastructure management.
motivation: Blockchain-as-a-Service (BaaS) models suffer from trust and flexibility issues due to third-party control; eBIM aims to restore trust by embedding blockchain management into open, verifiable hardware.
method: The paper surveys existing technologies and defines eBIM as a paradigm combining RISC-V with cryptographic acceleration, trusted execution environments, and smart contract engines.
result: It provides a conceptual framework and research directions but does not present experimental results or quantitative analysis.
conclusion: eBIM offers a promising direction for decentralized infrastructure management, but further implementation and evaluation are needed.

title: Unlearning To Protect: A Distilled Reinforcement Learning Framework With Privacy-Preserving Feature Unlearning And Xai For IoT Security
authors: Golam Rabiul Alam Md. Nahid Hasan
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07635v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Botnets pose a significant cybersecurity threat, enabling attacks such as DDoS, data theft, and service disruptions on IoT devices. These devices often lack built-in botnet traffic filtering, leaving them highly exposed. Existing AI-based solutions improve detection capabilities but have limitations: (i) they are too heavy for IoT deployment, and (ii) they lack unlearning capabilities to forget sensitive or outdated features without retraining. To address these challenges, we propose DiRLU, a lightweight, reinforcement learning driven framework, while ensuring privacy by selectively unlearning sensitive or outdated features without requiring retraining. The framework leverages knowledge distillation to transfer knowledge from a teacher model into a lightweight student model, with both models trained using A2C. A post-hoc unlearning mechanism modifies weights to remove targeted features, while restored features show negligible performance loss, confirming reversibility. Unlike many benchmark models that used only 5% of the BoT-IoT dataset, this research leverages 25%, allowing us to develop a strong teacher model. Both the teacher and student models were trained using the A2C reinforcement learning algorithm, achieving impressive results, with the student model achieving 99.60% accuracy and a 99.80% F1 score. To enhance transparency, we integrated Explainable AI (XAI), particularly LIME, which helps interpret the model's decisions and identify the key features influencing its predictions. Moreover, DiRLU requires only 2,370 FLOPS, approximately 3.87x more efficient than the state-of-the-art model, highlighting its efficiency for edge deployment. DiRLU combines efficiency with privacy, aligning with GDPR standards (right to be forgotten) to provide practical and scalable IoT security solution.
tldr: This paper proposes a reinforcement learning framework with feature unlearning and XAI for IoT botnet detection.
motivation: IoT devices are vulnerable to botnet attacks, and existing AI solutions are too heavy and lack privacy-preserving unlearning capabilities.
method: The framework uses knowledge distillation with A2C reinforcement learning, a post-hoc unlearning mechanism to remove sensitive features, and LIME for explainability.
result: The student model achieves 99.60% accuracy and 99.80% F1 score on 25% of the BoT-IoT dataset, requiring only 2,370 FLOPS.
conclusion: DiRLU provides a lightweight, privacy-preserving, and explainable solution for IoT security, aligning with GDPR standards.

title: Impact Of Courant Number On The Results Of Numerical Simulating Of Signal Propagation In Non-dispersive Homogeneous Media
authors: P. A. Makarov, R. N. Skandakov, V. A. Ustyugov, V. I. Shcheglov
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06707v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The paper is devoted to the study of the connection between the numerical dispersion arising in FDTD modeling of electromagnetic signal propagation in nondispersive homogeneous media optically different from vacuum and the Courant number in the 2D case. The main results are formulated in the form of four statements, as well as a number of corollaries and remarks that determine the nature of the numerical dispersion, the optimal value of the Courant number and the limitations of the method. It is proved that the optimal choice of the Courant number eliminates the numerical dispersion and extends the capabilities of the developed numerical algorithm to media, which refractive index lesser than refractive index of vacuum, as well as media with negative refraction.
tldr: This paper studies numerical dispersion in FDTD simulations of electromagnetic signal propagation, focusing on the optimal Courant number.
motivation: To understand and mitigate numerical dispersion in FDTD modeling of electromagnetic waves in non-dispersive homogeneous media.
method: The authors analyze the connection between numerical dispersion and the Courant number in 2D FDTD simulations, deriving optimal values and limitations.
result: They prove that an optimal Courant number eliminates numerical dispersion and extends the algorithm to media with refractive index less than vacuum or negative refraction.
conclusion: The optimal Courant number is crucial for accurate FDTD simulations, and the findings enable modeling of exotic media.

title: Will AstroForge Collapse The Pgm Market?
authors: Steven J. Smith Robert T. Nachtrieb
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06806v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AstroForge seeks to mine platinum group metals (PGM) from asteroids. Asteroid reserves appear to be unlimited, and at current market price the gross margin of asteroid mining would be very high. It is natural to ask: when AstroForge successfully demonstrates economic space mining of PGM, will they cause the PGM market to collapse? We answer the question with a non-steady system dynamics model of the PGM market. We find that the market price for PGM will eventually drop towards the much lower cost of asteroid mining, but only after the entire supply has shifted off-world. In the meanwhile, huge fortunes will be made. And everybody on Earth will benefit from new applications of lower-price PGM.
tldr: This paper models the economic impact of asteroid mining on the platinum group metals market.
motivation: To predict whether successful asteroid mining by AstroForge would collapse the PGM market.
method: A non-steady system dynamics model of the PGM market is used to simulate price evolution.
result: The market price drops to the cost of asteroid mining only after the entire supply shifts off-world, with large profits in the interim.
conclusion: Asteroid mining will not immediately collapse the market; instead, it will gradually replace terrestrial supply while generating huge fortunes.

title: Radiation Damage Cascades In Fullerite Using Molecular Dynamics
authors: Ethan P. Turner (department Of Physics And Astronomy Curtin University Perth WA 6845 Australia), Paolo Raiteri (school Of Molecular And Life Sciences Curtin University Perth WA 6845 Australia), Nigel A. Marks
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06962v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Molecular dynamics is used to study radiation cascades in solid C60 under ambient conditions. Simulations are performed for Primary Knock-On Atom (PKA) energies from 0.1 to 1 keV, and cascades are sampled over many PKA directions to collect statistics. Energies and forces are described using the Environment Dependent Interaction Potential for carbon paired with the Ziegler-Biersack-Littmark potential for short-range interactions, and cascade behaviour is characterized by tracking kinetic energy, hybridization and bond connectivity as a function of time. Compared to most materials, fullerite exhibits an unusual radiation response due to weak thermal transfer between C60 molecules leading to a thermalization phase lasting hundreds of picoseconds. The cascades damage the C60 molecules and link them together, and a linear relation is found between the number of cross-linked molecules and the number of new sp3 atoms. The threshold displacement energy computed is 18 eV, in agreement with experiments.
tldr: Molecular dynamics study of radiation damage cascades in solid C60 fullerite.
motivation: To understand the unusual radiation response of fullerite due to weak thermal transfer between C60 molecules.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations using Environment Dependent Interaction Potential and Ziegler-Biersack-Littmark potential for PKA energies 0.1-1 keV.
result: Cascades damage C60 molecules and link them; linear relation between cross-linked molecules and new sp3 atoms; threshold displacement energy 18 eV.
conclusion: Fullerite exhibits a thermalization phase lasting hundreds of picoseconds, and the radiation response is characterized by cross-linking and sp3 formation.

title: Integers In Sequences Generated By Recurrences With Non-Integer Coefficients
authors: Max Lippmann
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06573v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the properties of linear second-order recurrences whose coefficients are non-integer rational numbers. We examine the set of indices at which the terms in the sequence are integers. Specifically, we prove two results. First, after fixing coefficients to satisfy certain coprimality assumptions, we show that there exist coprime integer initial conditions so that the set of integer terms of that sequence is as large as desired. Second, using the same coprimality assumptions, for each fixed pair of initial conditions, we give an explicit cutoff index after which no further terms are integral.
tldr: This paper studies integer terms in linear recurrences with non-integer rational coefficients, a topic in number theory.
motivation: To understand when sequences generated by recurrences with non-integer coefficients produce integer terms.
method: Uses coprimality assumptions and explicit constructions to analyze the set of indices where terms are integers.
result: Proves that for fixed coefficients, there exist initial conditions making the integer set arbitrarily large, and gives a cutoff index after which no further integer terms occur.
conclusion: The behavior of integer terms in such recurrences can be controlled and bounded.

title: Realized Rank Certificates For Matchstick Frameworks And Insertion Edges
authors: Mike Winkler
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06576v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give an exact, checkable rank-certificate method for realized planar unit-distance frameworks. The method is motivated by Vogel's computations for matchstick graphs and by the insertion-edge tests used in the Matchstick Graphs Calculator. Its algebraic core is independent of geometry. A singular square matrix [MATH] is replaced by a sparse perturbation [MATH]. If [MATH] is nonsingular and the inverse satisfies [MATH], then the columns of [MATH] and the rows of [MATH] form bases of the right and left kernels of [MATH], and the rank defect of [MATH] is certified. Applied to the equilibrium matrix of a planar framework, this gives finite exact certificates for self-stresses, infinitesimal motions, redundant edges, and candidate edges whose constraints are already forced by the realized framework. The certificate data can be checked independently from the search that produced it, using exact matrix identities. We emphasize that matchstick frameworks are not generic: unit distances, triangles, rhombi, and symmetries can change the realized rank. The method therefore concerns the coordinate-dependent representation of a given drawing, not only the generic rigidity matroid of the abstract graph.
tldr: This paper presents a rank-certificate method for planar unit-distance frameworks, focusing on matchstick graphs and insertion edges.
motivation: To provide exact, checkable certificates for self-stresses, infinitesimal motions, and redundant edges in realized planar frameworks, addressing the non-generic nature of matchstick frameworks.
method: A singular square matrix is replaced by a sparse perturbation; if the perturbed matrix is nonsingular and its inverse satisfies certain conditions, the columns and rows of the original matrix form bases of the kernels, certifying the rank defect.
result: The method yields finite exact certificates for structural properties of planar frameworks, independent of geometry, and can be verified independently.
conclusion: The approach is effective for matchstick frameworks where unit distances and symmetries affect realized rank, but it is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Vieta-Type Formulas For Matrix Polynomials
authors: Shrinath Hadimani
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06606v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The classical Vieta formulas relate the coefficients of a complex scalar polynomial to the elementary symmetric polynomials of its roots. In this paper, we establish analogous spectral identities for complex matrix polynomials. For a monic matrix polynomial, we prove that the sum of all its eigenvalues equals the sum of the roots of the product of its diagonal scalar polynomials and is also equal to a constant multiple of the sum of the roots of the scalar polynomial obtained by summing its diagonal entries. We further show that the product of the eigenvalues of a monic matrix polynomial is determined by the determinant of its constant coefficient matrix. As a consequence, we recover the matrix Vieta formulas of Fuchs and Schwarz , for independent solutions of matrix algebraic equations via a density argument. We also derive corresponding identities for non-monic matrix polynomials with nonsingular leading coefficients and show, by means of an example, that the identities established for monic matrix polynomials do not extend directly to the non-monic case.
tldr: This paper extends Vieta's formulas to matrix polynomials, relating eigenvalues to coefficients.
motivation: To generalize classical Vieta formulas from scalar to matrix polynomials, providing spectral identities.
method: Uses algebraic manipulations and a density argument to prove identities for monic and non-monic matrix polynomials.
result: Establishes that sum of eigenvalues equals sum of roots of diagonal scalar polynomials, and product of eigenvalues is determined by determinant of constant term.
conclusion: The identities hold for monic matrix polynomials but do not directly extend to non-monic cases.

title: On The Polynomial Values Represented By Quadratic Forms
authors: Jamal Agbanwa Bogdan Grechuk
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06627v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many Diophantine equations can be reduced to the question of whether, for a given non-degenerate quadratic form [MATH] and a univariate polynomial [MATH] with integer coefficients, [MATH] can be represented by [MATH] for infinitely many values of [MATH]. We develop a method for answering this question for certain cubic and quartic polynomials [MATH], as well as for certain polynomials of the form [MATH], where [MATH] and [MATH] are polynomials of degree [MATH] and [MATH], respectively. Applying this method with [MATH], [MATH] and [MATH], we conclude that [MATH] is a sum of two squares infinitely often. In turn, this implies that the equation [MATH] has infinitely many integer solutions. Prior to this work, it was the shortest equation for which it was open whether its integer solution set is finite or infinite. We conclude with a list of the new shortest equations whose finiteness problem remains open. All main results of this paper has been formalized in Lean using Aristotle.
tldr: This paper studies Diophantine equations and polynomial values represented by quadratic forms, with no connection to quantum information theory.
motivation: To determine whether certain polynomial values can be represented by quadratic forms infinitely often, and to resolve the finiteness of integer solutions for short Diophantine equations.
method: Develops a method for cubic and quartic polynomials, and polynomials of the form f(g(x)), using quadratic forms and formalization in Lean.
result: Proves that n^4+2n^3+2n^2+n+1 is a sum of two squares infinitely often, implying the equation x^2+y^2 = n^4+2n^3+2n^2+n+1 has infinitely many integer solutions.
conclusion: The paper resolves the finiteness problem for the shortest previously open Diophantine equation and lists new shortest open equations.

title: A Scalable Linear Programming-based Framework For Data Clustering
authors: Aida Khajavirad, Huanwen Shen, Yakun Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06709v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend the linear programming-based algorithm of De Rosa et al~ for K-means clustering to two important clustering paradigms: fair K-means clustering and spectral clustering. For fair K-means clustering, we show that widely used notions of group fairness can be incorporated into the partition-matrix formulation of K-means clustering through a linear number of linear inequalities. For spectral clustering, we consider a linear programming relaxation of the minimum ratio-cut problem that fits naturally within the same framework. We complement these formulations with problem-specific initialization and rounding procedures and evaluate the resulting algorithms on a large collection of real-world data sets. Denoting by [MATH] the number of data points, our computational results demonstrate that the proposed approach solves [MATH] of benchmark instances with [MATH] to within [MATH] optimality in at most three hours. This in turn demonstrates the remarkable strength of the proposed LP relaxations in both applications. Moreover, for more than [MATH] of the instances, the proposed algorithm finds better solutions than those produced by popular fair Lloyd-type and spectral clustering heuristics.
tldr: This paper proposes a linear programming-based framework for fair K-means and spectral clustering, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to extend a linear programming approach for K-means clustering to fair clustering and spectral clustering, addressing practical data clustering problems.
method: They formulate fair K-means clustering by adding linear inequalities to the partition-matrix formulation, and spectral clustering via a linear programming relaxation of the minimum ratio-cut problem, with custom initialization and rounding.
result: The proposed LP relaxations solve 90% of benchmark instances to within 1% optimality in under three hours, often outperforming popular heuristics.
conclusion: The linear programming framework is effective for fair and spectral clustering, demonstrating strong performance on real-world datasets.

title: Linear-Quadratic Mean Field Games With Hybrid Local-Global Interactions On Manifolds
authors: Tao Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06742v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies linear-quadratic mean field games on compact Riemannian manifolds with a hybrid interaction topology. The network structure is a superposition of a deterministic graph for local geometric connectivity and a stochastic directed graph for non-local interactions. The global graph is constructed via random sampling based on a continuous kernel [MATH]. The out-degree of each node scales as [MATH] or as [MATH] to represent a sparse or dense network, respectively. In the infinite-population limit, the continuum system is governed by a coupled system of forward-backward partial differential equations, where the dynamics of the expected state incorporate the integral operator corresponding to the non-local sampling. The existence of a Nash equilibrium is established for this limit system. Furthermore, the approximation error is analyzed using operator concentration inequalities and analytic semigroup theory. Non-asymptotic high-probability error bounds between the finite-population empirical state and the continuum limit are derived. The convergence rates differ depending on the two topological regimes. Under the dense regime, the tracking error exhibits a polynomial decay rate dependent on the manifold dimension and Sobolev regularity, while under the sparse regime, the error decays at a rate of [MATH].
tldr: This paper studies linear-quadratic mean field games on manifolds with hybrid local-global interactions, which is unrelated to quantum information theory.
motivation: The paper aims to analyze mean field games with hybrid interaction topologies on Riemannian manifolds, a topic in game theory and stochastic control.
method: The authors model the network as a superposition of a deterministic graph for local interactions and a stochastic directed graph for non-local interactions, and derive a continuum limit described by forward-backward PDEs.
result: Existence of Nash equilibrium is established, and non-asymptotic error bounds between finite-population and continuum limit are derived, with convergence rates depending on network density.
conclusion: The work provides a mathematical framework for mean field games on manifolds with hybrid interactions, but has no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Adaptive, Matrix-Free Low-Rank Approximation
authors: Arnel I. Smith, Elly Do, Chao Chen
